newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.

text.p: The Malaysian interbank money market and interest rates futures market, the Malaysia Monetary Exchange, are closed on Wednesday for the Wesak Day holiday.
On Tuesday, interbank rates remained firm as banks kept funds for payment for a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Thursday, dealers said.
The overnight was traded between 15 and 20 percent, against 13/20 percent on Monday.
One- and two-week money were at 10.0/15.0 percent against 8.0/9.5 percent on Monday.
One-month money was at 9.0/9.5 percent and three- and six-month at 8.0/8.5 percent. They were all quoted at 7.5/8.0 percent previously.

The rise in interbank rates started last Thursday after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion worth of the dollar.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels. .
